text:
Thomas Harley played 30:54 against Florida on Nov 15 with Dallas down to five defensemen, and that's his season in one number: he's at 25:35 a night, rising past 26 lately, and the Stars keep asking for more.

He's answered with 10 points in his last ten games against 6.4 expected, so some of the recent burst is running hot. The latest was a late equalizer from distance in Vegas on Nov 19 that the Stars went on to win in a shootout; Jesse Granger of The Athletic noted it slipped through Adin Hill's glove.

The season overall is solid rather than spectacular: 15 points in 22 games, three goals right on his expected total, and Dallas takes about 53% of the five-on-five shot attempts with him on. Evolving-Hockey wasn't kind to his defense last season, with opponents getting more chances with him out there, so the defensive end is the thing to watch as the minutes climb.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows a defenseman who likes to jump into the rush: 28% of his shots come that way, against 17% for a typical D. He played for Canada at the 2026 Olympics.
